mail.purpose: The email address in the contact row.

body.purpose: Reading copy, capped at 31em, and the navigation links.

motion.name: nav-underline

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All three sit inside this query; without it nothing moves. There is no entrance or scroll-driven motion.

components.css: .ds-header { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: clamp(20px, 3vw, 44px); padding-block: 18px; font: 400 clamp(1rem, 0.94rem + 0.25vw, 1.125rem) / 1.55 var(--sans, 'Red Hat Text', 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif); color: var(--ink, #1d1612); } .ds-wordmark { margin-right: auto; font-family: var(--serif, 'Castoro', 'Iowan Old Style', Georgia, serif); font-size: 1.625rem; line-height: 1; color: var(--espresso, #3b1c09); text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; column-gap: clamp(18px, 2.6vw, 40px); } .ds-nav a { color: inherit; padding-block: 10px; text-decoration-thickness: 1px; text-underline-offset: 0.22em; text-decoration-color: transparent; } .ds-nav a:hover { text-decoration-color: currentColor; } .ds-header a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--olive, #394718); outline-offset: 3px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .ds-nav a { transition: text-decoration-color 0.2s; } }

components.name: Theme Switch
components.description: Round icon-only button with role=switch. The half-filled circle turns 180 degrees in the dark theme (keyed to data-theme on the page; shown here on aria-checked).
components.html: <button class="ds-switch" type="button" role="switch" aria-checked="false" aria-label="Dark theme"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.25"/><path d="M12 3.75a8.25 8.25 0 0 1 0 16.5z"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-switch { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 44px; height: 44px; padding: 0; border: 1px solid var(--rule, #ddd5cd); border-radius: 50%; background: none; color: var(--espresso, #3b1c09); cursor: pointer; } .ds-switch:hover { border-color: var(--ink-soft, #5c5047); } .ds-switch svg { width: 20px; height: 20px; fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.5; } .ds-switch path { fill: currentColor; stroke: none; } .ds-switch[aria-checked="true"] svg { transform: rotate(180deg); } .ds-switch:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--olive, #394718); outline-offset: 3px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .ds-switch svg { transition: transform 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } }

narrative.overview:
The site is a bakery counter seen in soft window light: a flour-white ground, espresso-brown lettering, and photographs of cast iron, cakes, linen and marble hung like prints with square corners. It is a familiar, clean, premium-homeware arrangement, chosen over louder graphic directions; the craft sits in proportion, type and light, not in ornament.

The page carries one idea, the company's plan in order, and the layout repeats it. The headline says kitchen goods first, then a bakery and café; under it the cast-iron pot fills the left half and the cakes and the café table sit on the right half, and the chapters row sets Forge Kitchen and the bakery and café in the same two halves. Everything hangs from one grid of four equal columns whose middle line is the page's single axis. Density is generous and calm: sections are separated by space, and the only rules on the page are the two hairlines above Company and Contact.

The system is authored twice. Light is flour and espresso; dark is a roasted brown ground with cream lettering, and olive turns from deep to pale so links keep their contrast. Photographs are AI-generated illustrations of mood and material and are labelled as illustrative.
keyCharacteristics: Flour ground, espresso headings, and one olive that belongs to links and focus.
Castoro for what the company says; Red Hat Text for what is read.
One four-column grid: headings and text start at the left margin or at the middle line.
Space separates sections; two hairlines are the only rules.
Square-cornered photographs over a paper tone; the one curve is the round theme switch.
Flat and still: no shadows, no tinted bands, no gradients, no entrance motion.
Light and dark themes are both first-class.

rules.name: The Olive Is a Link Rule
rules.body: Olive colours text that can be followed and the marks of focus: inline links, the focus ring, selection, the skip link. It is never a section field, a band, a bar or a heading colour. Navigation links and the wordmark stay ink and espresso.

rules.name: The One Ground Rule
rules.body: The whole page sits on flour. There is no second surface colour; paper appears only behind a photograph that has not loaded yet.

rules.name: The Dimmed Print Rule
rules.body: Photographs are never swapped per theme. In dark they are dimmed to 90% brightness.

rules.name: The Spoken and Read Rule
rules.body: Castoro carries what the company says in its own voice: the headline, section headings, the intro, the company statement, the wordmark and the email address. Red Hat Text carries what is read: paragraphs, navigation, captions, the footer.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: Everything is weight 400. Emphasis is a change of family or size.

rules.name: The Fluid Ramp Rule
rules.body: A new size is one of the seven steps. A size is written once and is not restated inside a breakpoint.

rules.name: The One Axis Rule
rules.body: In the main content, a heading or a block of text starts at the left margin or at the middle line of the four-column grid, and a photograph takes a quarter, a half or the full width. No block is centred or set on a third.

rules.name: The Space, Not Lines Rule
rules.body: Sections are separated by `space`. The hairlines above Company and Contact are the only dividing rules on the page; there are no vertical dividers, bands or bars.

rules.name: The No Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow would be the first one in the system.

rules.name: The Print Rule
rules.body: A photograph is a print: square corners, no border, no radius, no overlay text. Its caption note sits beneath it.

dos: Do start headings and text at the left margin or at the middle line of the four-column grid, and size photographs to a quarter, a half or the full width.
Do separate sections with `space`, and keep hairlines to the ruled rows.
Do keep photographs square-cornered at 3:2 (or as a pair inside a 3:2 box, or the 2:1 wide photograph), over `paper`, with a real `alt` and explicit width and height.
Do put the caption note under any photograph that could read as a product or a location.
Do author every colour in both themes, using the custom properties, and dim photographs in dark instead of replacing them.
Do take type sizes from the seven-step ramp.
Do keep all motion inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.
Do keep the navigation links visible at every width, and the 2px olive focus outline with its 3px offset.
Do put styles in `styles.css`; the content security policy blocks inline `style` attributes and third-party fonts and stylesheets.
Do write asset URLs in `styles.css` from the repository root (`assets/fonts/...`); the deploy script rewrites them.
donts: Don't use olive as a field, band, bar or heading colour; it belongs to links and focus.
Don't add a second accent colour or a second surface colour.
Don't divide with vertical lines, tinted bands or decorative bars.
Don't add shadows, blurs, gradients, or rounded corners on photographs.
Don't use bold; every style is weight 400.
Don't load fonts from a third-party host or add a third family.
Don't add entrance, scroll-driven or looping animation.
Don't swap photographs per theme; dim them.
Don't present an illustrative image as an actual Forge Kitchen product or an actual café.
